rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee whose home address is outside Switzerland is subject to source tax, whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland who is Swiss or holds a C permit is not subject. An employee living in Switzerland who is not Swiss and has no C permit is not subject if married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland. Every other employee is subject. Only employees subject to source tax are asked the source tax questions.
rules.expression: address_country != "Switzerland" or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type != "C permit" and not (civil_status == "Married" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "C permit") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"))

rules.name: Pension insurance start date
rules.statement: The insurance start date is derived from the latest confirmed first working day and is not asked. If the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month (e.g. first working day 15.03.2026 gives 01.04.2026). The result is always the 1st of a month, as the fund requires, in the format DD.MM.YYYY.

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: Define what Lonio asks a new employee during onboarding: which information, in which steps and order, and under which conditions - asking each piece of information once and reusing it for every receiving party.
feature.context:
HR calls the first working day the most important item. It often changes, so HR asks the employee to confirm it (F-TR-014, F-TR-015). The pension fund requires an insurance start date that is always the 1st of a month (F-SC-008, F-SC-009). HR works it out by hand: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day, otherwise on the 1st of the following month (F-TR-016, F-TR-017, F-TR-018). Once, an outdated first working day led to a wrong insurance start date at the fund (F-TR-019). Employees cannot know the insurance start date, so Lonio asks only for the primary fact and derives the date (G-08). The employee is not asked for the insurance start date (EX-05).

HR posts many documents to employees and needs the complete address as written on an envelope: street, number, postcode, town and country, with no extra parts (F-TR-009, F-TR-010). The country of the home address is also the employee's country of residence (F-TR-040, G-09). Several later questions depend on it. Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax (F-TR-034, F-TR-037), and the pension fund canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland. This feature therefore comes before the pension and source tax features that depend on it.

The pension fund portal requires first name, last name, date of birth, canton and civil status for every employee (F-SC-002 to F-SC-007, F-SC-010, F-SC-015). For married employees it also requires the spouse's date of birth and blocks the registration without it (F-TR-021, F-SC-012 to F-SC-014, F-SC-016). The civil status list shows only Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed (F-SC-011, G-07). HR's recollection of civil status matches the fund's list (F-TR-020, F-TR-022). Civil status is also an input for the source tax rule and the calculator (F-TR-029, F-TR-030). The fund offers only Swiss cantons and does not say whether it means the canton of residence or of work. Until the fund answers (OQ-02), the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland. It depends on address_country from FEAT-02. Registered partnerships, and portal behaviour for Divorced or Widowed, are still open.

HR decides by hand whether an employee is subject to source tax. Employees living abroad always are. Swiss nationals and C permit holders living in Switzerland are not. Other foreigners living in Switzerland are not subject if married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland (F-TR-005, F-TR-006, F-TR-025, F-TR-030, F-TR-034, F-TR-037). Data minimisation means each of these questions is asked only when its answer can change the outcome (G-01). The rule uses address_country (FEAT-02) and civil_status (FEAT-03). The tariff questions of the Zurich calculator have not been analysed yet (OQ-01, blocking). Until they are, this feature delivers the subject or not-subject decision that gates them. HR is not sure the rule is complete (OQ-05). The permit list is undefined (OQ-06). HR wished for a permit reminder because half of new employees forget to bring it (F-TR-028, OQ-07). Using the Zurich calculator for every employee is an agreed simplification (F-TR-008, G-05, OQ-08).

sections.title: Confirmed first working day and derived pension insurance start date
sections.purpose: Every new employee confirms their first working day, and Lonio works out the pension insurance start date from it, so the fund never gets a wrong or outdated start date.

stories.title: Employee confirms their first working day
stories.i_want: every new employee to confirm their first working day themselves during onboarding
stories.so_that: I always work with the latest agreed start date, even when it moved after the contract was signed, and can register the employee with the pension fund correctly
stories.priority_reason: HR calls it 'the number one thing'; it changes often, and an outdated date once caused a wrong registration at the pension fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-TR-014, F-TR-019).

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is asked of every employee and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is going through onboarding
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the employment details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked to confirm their first working day at Muster AG, whatever their other answers, and cannot finish onboarding without giving it

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee gives the date as actually agreed, as a calendar date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's start date may have moved since the contract was signed (e.g. they left their old employer a week earlier)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the first working day question
acceptance_criteria.then: they give the start date as currently agreed with Muster AG, as a full date in the form DD.MM.YYYY, so it reflects the latest confirmed first working day

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is available to HR and the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has confirmed their first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: onboarding data is handed on to the receiving parties
acceptance_criteria.then: HR receives the confirmed first working day, and it is the basis for the insurance start date the pension fund needs

stories.title: Insurance start date is derived from the confirmed first working day
stories.i_want: to receive an insurance start date that is the 1st of a month and follows from the employee's latest confirmed first working day
stories.so_that: the employee is insured from the correct date and registrations do not need weeks of correction
stories.priority_reason: The insurance start date is required for registration (F-SC-008); a wrong date already caused an incident with an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-TR-019).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee is not asked for the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is going through onboarding
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are never asked for an insurance start date; Lonio works it out from the confirmed first working day

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month: insurance starts that day
acceptance_criteria.given: the confirmed first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is the same day as the first working day

stories.i_want: to receive the new employee's first name, last name and date of birth
stories.so_that: I can register the employee for occupational pension without the registration being rejected for missing required fields
stories.priority_reason: These are required fields of the pension fund registration; if any is missing, the portal rejects the registration and highlights the field (F-SC-015), which blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and their last name; neither can be left empty, and both are made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked and required as a date
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their date of birth as a day, month and year (shown as DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 14.02.1990); it cannot be left empty and is made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Each detail is asked only once
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their name and date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: another part of the onboarding or another receiving party needs the same detail
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked for it again; the earlier answer is reused.

stories.title: Civil status from the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to receive the employee's civil status as one of the values my registration accepts
stories.so_that: I can register the employee and know whether spouse details apply
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required pension fund field; without it the registration is blocked (F-SC-010, F-SC-015). It is also an input for source tax (F-TR-029, F-TR-030).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the family details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their civil status; it cannot be left empty and is made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.when: they choose an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, as the pension fund lists them; no other values are offered. How employees in a registered partnership or another status (e.g. separated) answer is open (OQ-03).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is reused for source tax and HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax decision or the source tax questions need it
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer is reused and the employee is not asked again.

acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the employee's home address is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio does not ask for the employee's nationality, because employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality. Whether the Zurich calculator needs it after all is open (OQ-01).

stories.title: Ask the permit type only of non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: to be asked about my residence permit only if I live in Switzerland and am not Swiss
stories.so_that: HR can see whether I hold a C permit and, if I do, treat me like a Swiss national for source tax
stories.priority_reason: C permit holders are not subject to source tax (F-TR-025). Without the permit type they would be asked the source tax questions for no reason (F-TR-005).

acceptance_criteria.title: Permit type is asked and required for non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and their nationality is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks which Swiss residence permit the employee holds, the employee must answer it, and HR uses it to decide whether the employee is subject to source tax.

examples.name: Maria (F-TR-025), Portuguese, assumed to live in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Permit type is not asked of Swiss employees or employees living abroad
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is Swiss, or lives outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio does not ask for a permit type, because the answer cannot change the source tax decision.

acceptance_criteria.title: Permit choices and permit reminder are still open
acceptance_criteria.given: the sources name only the B permit and the C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the permit question is shown to the employee
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers include at least "B permit" and "C permit". The full list of permit types is still open (OQ-06). For the source tax decision, only C permit versus any other answer matters. HR wants the questionnaire to remind employees to bring their permit, but whether to add the reminder and its wording are still open (OQ-07).

stories.title: Ask spouse details only when they can exempt the employee
stories.i_want: Lonio to collect the spouse's nationality, permit and country of residence only from married employees whose own status would otherwise make them subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to check the spouse case by hand and collect spouse details by email
stories.priority_reason: Today HR checks this case by hand and collects the details by email, which 'takes forever' (F-TR-033). Without the spouse details, employees like Tomás are wrongly treated as subject to source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality is asked only when the spouse can change the outcome
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is married, lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and does not hold a C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the spouse's nationality and the employee must answer it. Lonio does not ask it of any other employee, including employees who are married but Swiss, hold a C permit or live abroad. HR uses the answer for the source tax decision.

examples.name: Single B permit holder in Switzerland
Married C permit holder in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's permit type is asked only for a non-Swiss spouse and may be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality is needed (AC-04.3.1) and the spouse is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the spouse's Swiss residence permit, if they have one. The employee may leave it empty if the spouse has no permit. Lonio does not ask it if the spouse is Swiss. The list of permit types is open (OQ-06).

examples.name: B permit holder with an Italian spouse

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's country of residence is asked only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality is needed (AC-04.3.1)
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks where the spouse lives and the employee must answer it. Lonio does not ask it if the spouse is neither Swiss nor a C permit holder, because then the spouse cannot exempt the employee.

examples.name: Spouse is Italian with a C permit
Spouse is Italian with a B permit

stories.title: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax
stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from the employee's answers whether they are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I know up front who has to answer the source tax questions, and Swiss employees and other exempt employees are not bothered with them
stories.priority_reason: HR never knows up front who has to answer the source tax questions, and Swiss employees get annoyed and call HR (F-TR-005). This decision controls whether the whole source tax step is asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the employee's home address is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides on source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax, whatever their nationality.

acceptance_criteria.title: Swiss nationals and C permit holders living in Switzerland are not subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax. C permit holders are treated like Swiss nationals.

examples.name: Maria (F-TR-025), Portuguese with a C permit, assumed to live in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse exemption for other foreigners living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and does not hold a C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides on source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject only if they are married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and who lives in Switzerland. In every other case the employee is subject.

examples.name: Tomás (F-TR-030), Brazilian, B permit, Swiss wife in Winterthur
Spouse is Italian with a C permit and lives in Switzerland
Spouse is Italian with a B permit
Single B permit holder in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: only employees who are subject are asked the source tax tariff questions; employees who are not subject are not asked them. The tariff questions themselves (including the different questions for married employees and the extra questions for employees living abroad) are not yet defined (OQ-01, blocking). For now, the Zurich calculator applies to every subject employee (OQ-08).

acceptance_criteria.title: Rule completeness to be confirmed by HR
acceptance_criteria.given: HR hedged on whether the rule is complete ('I think that's it')
acceptance_criteria.when: the decision rule is released
acceptance_criteria.then: HR has checked the decision rules against real cases (Stefan, Maria, Tomás). Any missing case is handled through OQ-05, not by inventing new rules.
